approved: Clean Energy Finance Corporation Amendment (Grid Reliability Fund) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would create a $1 billion Grid Reliability Fund to be run by the Clean Energy Finance Corporation.
The fund would be held in a new Special Account and used for investments in energy generation, storage, transmission and grid-stabilising technologies.
Investments from the fund would be exempt from the usual requirement that at least half of the corporation's funds go to renewable energy projects.
Establishes a $1 billion Grid Reliability Fund through a new Special Account.
Creates a new investment category for the fund.
Expands the definition of low-emissions technologies to cover those announced for the fund.
Allows regulations to prescribe additional investment types for the fund.
Gives the Clean Energy Finance Corporation new functions to assist Commonwealth agencies with grid reliability policies.
Exempts fund investments from the 50 per cent renewable energy investment requirement.
The Clean Energy Finance Corporation and energy market participants, including new and smaller generators.

The Morrison government's $1 billion Grid Reliability Fund was introduced to support private investment in energy generation, storage and transmission, aiming to lower electricity prices, reduce emissions and create jobs. The fund will back projects including pumped hydro, batteries and gas-fired generation, but not coal, and builds on Australia's record 6.3 gigawatts of new renewable capacity installed in 2019.

The Labor Party argued the Clean Energy Finance Corporation Amendment (Grid Reliability Fund) Bill 2020 would undermine the CEFC's independence, allow ministerial direction, classify gas as low-emissions technology, and remove the requirement for positive returns. They announced they would move amendments to protect these principles and would only support the bill if those amendments are accepted, noting the CEFC has deployed $6 billion, leveraged $27.3 billion in private investment, and funded 18,000 projects.

The Morrison government announced a $1 billion Grid Reliability Fund, administered by the Clean Energy Finance Corporation, to support investments in new energy generation, storage and transmission, and outlined five stretch goals for low-emission technology including clean hydrogen under $2 per kilogram and energy storage under $100 per megawatt hour.
